Zuma's New Jet

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
This is the story the impeding lease or purchase of a mnew wide bodies plane for the exclusive use of the president. At present Zuma uses a specially fitted Boeing 737 for his person usage and which has been hit by snags, resulting in the president not wanting to use that plane anymore. The irony is that a miuch older plane is being hired for him now. There is nothing wrong with the present plane, it has been hit by some maintenance issue and the question during the show will be why? Is it due to the fact that the last of the Denel engoners have been layed off/

The cost of a new wide bodies plane will be in the excess of 4 billion rand and that cost includes all the specialist fittings. Already commentators are sayint that Squadron 21 which oversees the VIparicraft takes up most of the airforce defence budget leaving very little for the purchase of other planes, the SA airforce needs. For example, the SANDF has to hire plans to transport troops.


Further information:
The insert will detail all the VIP planes. It will describe the Govt’s reasoning for a new plane, ostensibly to be ale to fly long disncatcnes instead of stopping for feul in Africa somewhere. It will describe the hierarchy on maintenance procedures – which are 1) squadron 21 small repairs. 2) Exucujet 3) SA airline maintenacce. We will describe that there is nothing inherently wrong with the present plane. It just need sto be maintained properly.

We also also describe how the present plane which is for the sole use of the president needs to fly as often as possible. When it stands still, it picks up problems. This is with all planes. We will ask the question – is this a nice to have, or a need? That set against the backdrop of a recission in this coutry, the fact that the airforce wil have to ask treasury for more money, and that most of the ariforce bidget is taken up by squadron 21, who is respobsible ofr the vip llanes.

To repeat – the govt says that the present plane is not safe. It should be in that it is a young plane. Therehave been some snags but not major snags, and snags that still allow for it to be sued after quick maintencce. What will change then if a new plane is bought? Nothing really. Those ianaintnce issues may well continue. Just a huge bill to play for a new plane/

To interview:
Dean wingrin - forensic auditor, creator of unofficial sa airforce website. Writer. Expert.
Darren Oliver – African defence review
Miss Gonson – Rapport – journliast, expert on planes, was in the defecne force.
Spokesperson from Squadron 21
Hopefully a ex Denel engineer.

Mr. Dean Wingrin
Mr. Darren Olivier
Ms. Erika Gibson
Mr. Kobus Marais

Press Release:


NO PRESS RELEASE ISSUED.
(Synopsis: This is the story of the impeding lease or purchase of a new wide bodied plane for the exclusive use of the president. At present Zuma uses a specially fitted Boeing 737 for his personal use and which has been hit by snags, resulting in the president not wanting to use that plane anymore. The irony is that a much older plane is being hired for him now. There is nothing wrong with the present plane, it has been hit by some maintenance issues and the question during the show will be why? Is it due to the fact that the last of the Denel engineers have been laid off?

Script:


Recently president Jacob Zuma flew in a charted gulfstream jet to attend the g20 summit in china, and on the 17th of September he flew over to New York in a SA airways passenger airbus airliner to attend the United Nations general assembly. The big question – why was he not using Inkwazi, filmed here landing in berlin last year, carrying him.


It’s a Boeing 737 luxurious business jet; it has extra fuel tanks in the hold to allow it to fly anywhere in Africa and most European countries without refueling.


Capt. Bruce Hyde is at the control of the same type of plane, a Boeing 737 and is taking off from Cape Town international airport, destination Johannesburg.

This 737 is 15 year old and has got at least another 20 years to go

Bruce Hyde: it has an impeccable safety record over its 40 plus years of existence. It’s a sophisticated commercial jet airliner.

Captain Hyde’s 737 is the same age but has done far more trips than Inkwazi. But it seems that the president is no longer using Inkwazi. And now controversy has erupted. Armscor issued tenders for the leasing or purchase of another jet for him, which includes a wide-bodied intercontinental plane capable of flying to any destination around the world without stopping for fuel.

Kobus Marais: so to buy a second one and then even consider a bigger one, intercontinental aircraft, it is just ludacris.

Aviation experts agree that because of SA's geographical location a presidential pane is required. But whilst our president has been using a 737 a country such as Denmark with a higher GDP makes use of a smaller Learjet.



On the 13th of September the minister offence (and military veterans) announced that until a wide-bodied plane was obtained, another jet would be leased for the president, costing r100 million. Aviation experts put that figure at 500 million rand.

Minister: it’s a non-negotiable matter. It has to be done. We can’t continue to risk the lives of our principals.

So is Inkwazi unsafe? Let’s take a look at its history, and the other jets used by vvips. Inkwazi is part maintained and operated by 21 squadron of the SA air force. This unit has several older smaller jets in its stable - a falcon 900, two falcon 50s and two citation jets which are for the use of the president, deputy president, various ministers and senior military officers.

Link: both former presidents f.w. De klerk and nelson Mandela used the falcon aircraft to travel both domestically and internationally. Then in 2001,2002 during the Mbeki presidency a Boeing business jet was purchased.

Erica Gibson, once a major in the SA air force is up to date on how the vvip planes were used during the Mbeki administration.

Erika: the falcon 50 for local, national. The falcon 900 elsewhere in the continent and Inkwazi would be used for transcontinental and that was how it was used.

As with any other (commercial) jet liner in the world, technical snags do creep in.

Link: of the technical issues encountered by Inkwazi, three have made headlines. Arguably the most prominent of those was a fuel leak picked up in Doha in the Middle East.

Then there was a stuck valve on one of the fuel tanks returning from Russia in may last year. An oil leak in in Burundi in Feb. This year. Neither was seen as safety critical issues.

Erika: the last that we wrote that he refused to fly, it was denied by the department of defense saying he didn’t refuse to fly, he just demanded a trustworthy aircraft that would not let him down.

Ever since the technical issues experienced with Inkwazi in may, the president has flown almost exclusively on a chartered Boeing 727 at a considerable expense. Erica however says that Inkwazi is safe to fly.

Erika: it’s standing at waterkloof. They do training on it. Some generals use it for some trips and so on. There is nothing wrong with it.

During the time president Zuma was flying around in his charted 727, a plane-tracking app detected 32 flights by Inkwazi, since June, presumably safe for who ever was flying in it. And the app also shows that on the same day that the chartered 727 carried the president to Gaborone on the 27th of June this year, Inkwazi made an internal flight.


So who is in charge of maintenance of Inkwazi? Well it’s split between 21 squadron and execujet.

We asked execujet if Inkwazi was safe to fly but they said they were bound by confidentially and referred us to the SA defense force. They too were not prepared to answer any questions saying that it may interfere the process of procuring a new jet. Questions sent to the office of the presidency were not responded to.



Now the da has now put in a pie application to execujet in order to get to the bottom of this story.

John: so if you gain access to these documents, what are you thinking it will tell you about Inkwazi?
Kobus Marais: well we truly believe that the arguments that they have used to consider buying a new aircraft is not valid and we believe that the argument of pure maintenance and reliability of Inkwazi is not valid at all.

Darren Olivier is a senior correspondent for a specialist defence security online publication - he has been writing regularly on this sage.


Darren: Inkwazi is maintained to a very strict maintenance regime, sat down by Boeing. There really is no way that Inkwazi is maintained badly, that I can tell. The air force is highly professional, the companies involved are professional and there are the skills.


It addition, it seems that the government has its eyes on a wide bodied plane similar to this one, possibly a wide bodied airbus from south African airways, we don’t know the costs. Experts are saying that it could be in the region of 20 million dollar extra to refurbish it. Operational costs will be much higher than Inkawai.

They are asking if these additional costs are worth it for the luxury of the president being able to fly non-stop to a handful of countries such as china, Russia and the USA.

Erika: former president Mbeki didn’t mind to stop from time to time for refueling. Mandela didn’t mind doing that. That was no problem then.


As things stand 21 squadron who own, part maintain and operate Inkwazi and the other vvip jets is most expensive single unit in the air force dwarfing even that of 2 squadron, with its 26 grippons. This concerns Dean Wingrin, author, defense journalist and creator of an unofficial SA air force website.

Dean: the budget exceeds such critical components not only of air defense but the search and rescue helicopter squadrons, the transport squadrons, the vital maritime surveillance anti poaching patrols that the air force has to perform with 50-year-old aircraft.

Darren: when the rest of the divorce is struggling for money, and old aircraft need to be replaced, it really is irresponsible to be spending that much money on what is effectively at the moment a nice to have.


Back from job, Capt. Hyde prepares for a smooth landing. But expect some turbulence ahead especially if the da is able to get their hands on Inkwazi’s maintenance records via their pie application. In the mean time Dean Wingrin too is questioning whether a big fancy wide bodied plane for the presidency is a must have or a nice to have or a nice to have
